subject: Mutual action plan & PoC sprint — deployment mode decision (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)
messages:
From: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Gomez <alyssa.gomez@clarityhealth.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@clarityhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Mutual action plan & PoC sprint — deployment mode decision (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)

Hi Alyssa / Tom —

Thanks again for yesterday’s call. Quick recap and a proposed mutual-action-plan so we can lock the deployment mode and get a PoC running next week. Key points I noted from the call:
- Data residency & PHI: Clarity needs logs/auditability and the ability to enforce KMS keys.
- Connectivity: you prefer VPC peering over public egress for network isolation.
- Performance: spikes during batch processing windows (batch of claims ingestion) — target is 99th p95/p99 latency constraints.

Options we discussed (brief):
- Hosted API: fastest to get started, limited to application-level encryption and Redwood-managed keys. Good for initial functional tests.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pool with private peering + customer KMS keys — lower latency, predictable throughput, good fit if you want a managed path with isolation.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): full private control plane, on-prem option for air-gapped or stricter compliance. More setup but aligns with strict audit requirements.

To move forward I propose a 3-week PoC sprint with two parallel tracks depending on your appetite to commit:
- Track A (preferred quick path): Dedicated capacity + VPC peering + customer KMS. Goal: prove throughput, latency, and integration with existing data pipeline.
- Track B (conservative): Hosted API with strict contract controls while we finalize networking and procurement; can flip to Dedicated mid-sprint if procurement moves faster than expected.

Can you confirm the following so we can finalize the MAP spreadsheet?
1) Which track do you want to start with (Track A / Track B)?
2) Primary success criteria (I suggest: ingest pipeline end-to-end, p99 inference latency < 250ms for 512-token prompts, throughput X requests/min sustained over 15 minutes, logs/audit accessible via S3 + KMS).
3) PO & procurement timeline (we’ll need a short-term commitment for Dedicated reservation if you pick Track A).
4) Stakeholders to loop for infra & security (Tom / Sana / procurement contact).

I’ve attached an initial MAP workbook and a short SOC2 summary for your security team. Ben and Karthik are looped for technical clarifications. Once you confirm track + criteria I’ll share a detailed sprint plan (owners, deliverables, test harness).

Thanks —
Maya
Maya Srinivasan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
maya@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0182

Attachments: MAP_ClarityHealth_v1.xlsx (MAP workbook), SOC2-summary.pdf (security overview)

Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 16:48:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan & PoC sprint — deployment mode decision (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)

Maya —

Thanks for the clear recap. We’re leaning toward Track A (Dedicated capacity with VPC peering and our KMS) because of the PHI exposure and audit requirements. A few clarifications from our side:

- Our security team (Sana Patel) wants to review the SOC2 summary and network template before we sign off on peering. I’ve CC’d procurement and Tom (platform lead).
- Procurement: we can do a short-term commitment for a 4-week reserved slot to cover the PoC, but we need cost estimates for that 4-week window and a clean statement of what changes if we convert to a longer reserved contract.
- Success criteria: we agree on end-to-end ingestion and auditability. Please add: ability to revoke keys and verify that KV cache isn’t stored outside the leased pool. Also include throughput target: sustain 200 reqs/min with 512-token avg and p99 < 300ms.

Timeline: can you run the sprint starting the week of Nov 16th? Tom and I can commit engineer time the week of Nov 16–27. Procurement hopes to get a PO to you by Nov 20th if costs are reasonable.

Next steps from our side: Sana will send a short list of compliance questions by EOD Tuesday. Procurement will follow up with billing contact details.

—Alyssa
Alyssa Gomez
Director, Platform Engineering, Clarity Health
alyssa.gomez@clarityhealth.com | +1 650-555-0833

Alyssa / team —

Helpful to summarize technical tradeoffs and what we’ll need to run Track A (Dedicated) smoothly. Short version: Dedicated + VPC peering + customer KMS will meet the majority of your compliance asks while minimizing setup time vs a full Private deployment. A few notes and what I’ll deliver this week:

1) What we’ll provision for PoC (Dedicated):
- 2x reserved GPU workers (N5-equivalent) in a dedicated pool with autoscale headroom for spikes.
- Private peering config — we’ll provide network-config-template.docx.
- KMS integration: allow customer-managed keys for S3 logs and model key wrapping.

2) Test harness & acceptance tests I’ll include:
- Throughput test: sustained 200 reqs/min for 30 minutes using your ingestion pattern.
- Latency profile: record p50/p95/p99 for 512-token prompts; target p99 < 300ms.
- Auditability checks: S3 logs + signed events, proof of KMS key usage and rotation.

3) Required inputs from Clarity:
- Network ranges & firewall allowlist for peering (I’ll provide the template).
- KMS ARN and service account that will rotate keys.
- A small sample dataset (anonymized) for functional validation — we’ll keep it in a short-lived S3 bucket.

4) Fallback plan: If procurement slips, we can stand up the same tests against Hosted API (no customer KMS) to validate functional behavior; we’ll clearly mark the differences in the MAP.

I’ve attached the network template and the SOC2 summary for Sana’s review. I’ll also attach a short cost estimate for a 4-week reserved slot and what a month-to-month conversion looks like.

Let me know if you want a quick call with the infra folks this week to walk through firewall rules.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com | +1 510-555-0124

Attachments: network-config-template.docx, SOC2-summary.pdf

Alyssa / Tom / team —

Appreciate the confirmation. Below is the mutual action plan (MAP) we’ll use as the working contract for the PoC. I pasted the high-level deliverables here and updated the MAP workbook (attached).

Mutual Action Plan — Clarity Health PoC (Track A: Dedicated)
- Sprint window: Nov 16 — Dec 4, 2026 (3 weeks active + wrap).
- PoC owner (Redwood): Ben Carter — setup, test harness, performance reporting.
- PoC owner (Clarity): Tom Reynolds — infra lead; Sana Patel (security) — compliance sign-off; procurement contact: procure@clarityhealth.com.
- Deliverables:
  * Week 0 (pre-work, Nov 9–15): exchange network ranges, KMS ARN, sample dataset; Redwood shares AWS peering instructions and cost estimate.
  * Week 1 (Nov 16–20): Dedicated pool provisioned + VPC peering established; run baseline functional tests.
  * Week 2 (Nov 23–27): Scale tests, throughput validation (200 reqs/min sustained), latency profiling (target p99 < 300ms).
  * Week 3 (Nov 30–Dec 4): Integration verification, auditability checks, handoff docs, decision checkpoint.
- Success criteria (must satisfy all to pass PoC):
  1) End-to-end ingestion and inference validated on anonymized sample data.
  2) p99 inference latency for 512-token prompts <= 300ms under defined load.
  3) Logs and audit trail accessible in Clarity’s S3 with customer KMS and rotation proof.
  4) No KV cache leakage outside dedicated pool; write-up and demo.
  5) Procurement provides a PO or written commitment for the 4-week reservation by Nov 20th (or we run Hosted fallback tests).

Attachments: MAP_ClarityHealth_v1.xlsx (updated with owners and dates), SOC2-summary.pdf, network-config-template.docx.

Next cadence: 30-min technical kickoff on Mon, Nov 16 at 10:00am PT — will send calendar invite once you confirm. If procurement can’t provide PO by Nov 20 we’ll run functional validation on Hosted and preserve data/metrics for a smooth cutover to Dedicated.

If this looks good I’ll update the HubSpot deal and share access to the MAP workbook.

Thanks —
Maya
